lesson.robot_structure_study.title: Robot Structure & Joints
lesson.robot_structure_study.summary: Construct a three-quarter robot from connected masses, compare near and far limbs, and layer joints so the design feels structurally believable.
lesson.robot_structure_study.step.mass_a: Build separate head, torso and pelvis masses, then use one body axis to keep their turn consistent.
lesson.robot_structure_study.help.mass_a: Let the masses change width slightly instead of stacking identical boxes.
lesson.robot_structure_study.complete.ma: The main masses now share a clear three-quarter direction.
lesson.robot_structure_study.step.near_f: Build a broader near arm and a smaller far arm, breaking each into upper-arm and forearm forms.
lesson.robot_structure_study.help.near_f: Use overlap at the shoulders and elbows so each arm feels connected instead of drawn as one line.
lesson.robot_structure_study.complete.ne: The arm sizes and overlaps create convincing depth.
lesson.robot_structure_study.step.weight: Construct two legs with different widths and angles, then plant the feet so the robot carries weight.
lesson.robot_structure_study.help.weight: The near leg can be broader and the far foot can be smaller and less exposed.
lesson.robot_structure_study.complete.we: The legs now support the body with a clear stance.
lesson.robot_structure_study.step.joint_: Add a few joint rings and a chest panel that sit on top of the larger forms.
lesson.robot_structure_study.help.joint_: Keep details subordinate to the main masses. A joint should explain a connection, not become decoration everywhere.
lesson.robot_structure_study.complete.jo: Your layered joints finish the structural robot study.
